Grade 3 thrombocytopenia during chemoimmunotherapy is stated, but the same paragraph says the patient reported no adverse events during the treatment.
The immunohistochemistry list prints "partial response (PR; 90%+)" immediately after ER; the source does not say that PR here means progesterone receptor.
MSH6 is printed as negative in the case text but described as a partial loss in the discussion.
The PD-L1 score is printed as GPS in the source.

The cardiac metastasis is called confirmed in the diagnosis sentence, but the discussion states pathological confirmation of the cardiac lesion was not obtained and that a cardiac thrombus or benign cardiac mass cannot be entirely ruled out; it also describes extrinsic compression whereas the echocardiogram describes a mass attached to the walls with mild protrusion into the cavity.

Response is described with different degrees and sources: right cardiac mass vanished (imaging in November 2024), near-total resolution of the myocardial metastasis (cardiac CT November 12, 2024), partial regression versus marked regression of pulmonary disease, partial regression versus resolution of the urethral lesion, and complete radiographic resolution after maintenance (Table 2, discussion).
The abstract gives the duration of bleeding as over 8 months and the case text as the past 8 months.
